item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports testing elapsed-time features inside BERT4Rec, but does not establish gains for this Amazon benchmark. Ti-CoRe (2026) directly adds time-interval-aware attention to BERT4Rec through a T-BERT encoder; reported improvements come from mobile-app data and a method also using contrastive augmentation, so they do not isolate the temporal component’s benefit here. [Ti-CoRe](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cpe.70585). TemProxRec (2024) combines absolute/relative temporal and positional embeddings with contrastive learning across interactions occurring in similar periods. Its useful distinction: within-user elapsed time versus shared calendar-time trends. [TemProxRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784).\n\nSession evidence is more indirect. Sequential Masked Modeling (2024) reports improvements from sliding windows and penultimate-token masking on session datasets; this supports examining training context and masking, but does not demonstrate that timestamp-derived session boundaries improve BERT4Rec. [Transformer-SMM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11150). A suitable experiment, inferred from these findings: retain one bidirectional transformer per category and compare position-only inputs against learned, bucketed time-gap attention biases, then an optional same-session bias inferred from observed history gaps. Allow temporal effects to increase or decrease attention rather than imposing recency decay. Preserve masked-target training and appended-mask inference; use only observed historical timestamps, with a distinct unknown-time representation for the appended mask. Do not supply the held-out target timestamp. Select through the fixed macro validation HR@10; published improvements provide hypotheses, not expected benchmark gains."}
